## The question

Three campaign runs share an input complex, a design count and every downstream
setting. They differ only in the contig string, so any difference in what
RFdiffusion builds is attributable to how the design regions were chosen.

| run | regions | designed residues | how the regions were chosen |
|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| `crystal_full_test_contig` | 2 | 16–26 | hand-picked, two contiguous blocks |
| `crystal_auto5A_contig` | 4 | 21–45 | auto-derived from effector contact at 5 Å |
| `crystal_auto3A_contig` | 6 | 10–19 | auto-derived from effector contact at 3 Å |

The `posed_*` runs are excluded, since they change the input structure as well as
the contig. `crystal_full_r1_17to21_contig` is excluded because it varies only the
allowed length of one region, which is the within-strategy question rather than
the between-strategy one.

Everything below reads `data/<run>.json`, the per-run `rfdiffusion_metrics.json`
the pipeline already writes, so nothing is recomputed from structures.

```{python}
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path.cwd()
if not (HERE / "novelty_common.py").exists():
    HERE = Path("experiments/campaigns/pikp1_avrpikf/analyses/design_region_novelty")
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.resolve()))

import novelty_common as nc  # noqa: E402

nc.apply_style()
regions = nc.load_regions()
designs = nc.load_designs()
```

---

## Where the design regions sit

Length and placement are different arguments and the summary tables only carry
length, so the contig strings are drawn directly.

```{python}
#| label: fig-contig-map
#| fig-cap: "The three contig strategies along wild-type Pikp-1 HMA numbering. Grey is retained scaffold, colour is rebuilt. Labels give the allowed length range for each design region."
_ = nc.fig_contig_map()
```

* The two strategies are not simply coarse and fine versions of each other. `full`
  rebuilds one large block in the middle of the domain and the C terminus, while
  both auto strategies scatter regions across the whole length.
* `auto 3 Å` has the most regions but the fewest designed residues, because four
  of its six regions are one or two residues wide.

---

## Displacement tracks length, but not equally between strategies

```{python}
#| label: fig-com-vs-length
#| fig-cap: "Centre-of-mass displacement of each rebuilt region against its length, pooled over designs and regions. One point per (design, region)."
from IPython.display import Image
Image(str(nc.PLOTS / "03_com_vs_length.png"))
```

* Displacement rises with region length across the pooled data, so any comparison
  between strategies has to account for the fact that they allow different lengths.
* The strategies do not merely occupy different parts of that trend. `full` forms
  a tight, almost linear band, whereas both auto strategies spread widely at every
  length, including at one and two residues where there is very little to rebuild.

---

## How much of that displacement is the scaffold moving?

Displacement is measured after aligning on the retained scaffold, so it only means
"the region was rebuilt somewhere new" if the scaffold itself held still.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-motif
#| tbl-cap: "Retained-scaffold RMSD to the input, per strategy."
(designs.groupby("run", sort=False)
        .agg(designs=("design", "size"),
             median_total_designed=("total_designed", "median"),
             median_motif_rmsd=("motif_rmsd", "median"),
             median_coverage=("design_region_coverage", "median"))
        .round(3))
```

* The retained scaffold barely moves under `full`, at a median motif RMSD of
  0.07 Å, but moves 2.6 Å and 4.0 Å under `auto 3 Å` and `auto 5 Å`.
* Part of the auto strategies' apparent displacement is therefore the domain
  drifting rather than the region being rebuilt somewhere novel, so the scatter in
  the previous figure overstates how much extra novelty they buy.

---

## Placement within a strategy

```{python}
#| label: fig-com-by-region
#| fig-cap: "Centre-of-mass displacement per design region, grouped by strategy. Regions are numbered N to C along the receptor."
Image(str(nc.PLOTS / "01_com_displacement_by_region.png"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-regions
#| tbl-cap: "Per-region length and displacement, by strategy."
(regions.groupby(["run", "region"], sort=False)
        .agg(n=("design", "size"), median_length=("length", "median"),
             median_com=("com_displacement", "median"),
             median_com_per_res=("com_per_residue", "median"))
        .round(3).reset_index())
```

* Displacement varies more between regions within a strategy than it does between
  strategies, and the C-terminal region moves furthest in all three, at 3.7, 7.2
  and 6.1 Å.
* That region is terminal and anchored on one side only, so placement rather than
  length is what frees it, which is the same conclusion the per-residue column
  reaches for the single-residue regions of `auto 3 Å`.

---

## Does region length change how varied the designs are?

Region 1 has a 10-20 residue allowance, so RFdiffusion picked a different length
in different designs. Comparing across those lengths is free of any between-run
or between-region confound, unlike the three-strategy comparison in
the three-strategy comparison above.

Diversity is the mean nearest-neighbour distance between two designs' Ca
coordinates for the same region, which is defined when the two have different
residue counts. Each design is compared only with designs that came out the same
length. Comparing against the whole pool instead gives a spurious U, because
RFdiffusion sampled lengths unevenly around 15 and the extremes then score as
distant for being a minority rather than for varying among themselves.

Numbers here use the `.trb`-corrected residue mapping. The pipeline's own
`per_region_lengths` are a proportional guess, wrong for most designs of any
contig with several variable-length regions. See `trb_metrics.py`.

```{python}
from IPython.display import Image
Image("plots/11_length_vs_diversity.png")
```

* Diversity rises with the length RFdiffusion built, from 0.65 Å at 10 residues
  to 1.14 Å at 20, or +7.0% per added residue. A quadratic term is not supported
  (p = 0.65), so there is no optimum length within the allowance.
* The per-design fit gives p = 5e-07, but designs of one length share pairwise
  distances, so the honest test is at the length-group level. That gives
  rho = +0.71 over the 11 lengths, p = 0.015.

* The C-terminal region is more varied than region 1 at any length, 2.31 Å on 6
  residues, which is expected for a region anchored on one side only. The two do
  not overlap in length, so this is a direction rather than a matched comparison.
* The retained scaffold held to 0.07 Å across all 64 designs, so none of the
  above is the fixed framework moving. All 64 designs build the same
  strand-loop-strand topology, so extra residues lengthen the connecting loop
  rather than adding elements.

```{python}
print(open("length_diversity_stats.txt").read())
```

## What this supports

* Design region choice does change what RFdiffusion builds, but region length is
  the weaker lever. Anchoring is the stronger one, and the clearest single
  comparison is the C-terminal region against interior regions of the same length.
* Larger contiguous regions buy displacement without disturbing the retained
  scaffold. Fragmented regions buy displacement partly by letting the scaffold
  move, which is not the kind of novelty the pipeline wants.

Caveats.

* One input complex and one effector, 64 designs per strategy. The contig strings
  differ in placement and in length at once, so no single comparison isolates
  either on its own.
* Centre-of-mass displacement says where a region ended up, not what it looks
  like. Two very different backbones with the same centroid are indistinguishable
  here.
* The auto strategies' motif RMSD means their displacement is measured in a frame
  that itself moved, so their values are not on the same footing as `full`'s.
